headline: Applicants withdrew the 50 Park Street application; agreed on a three-minute limit per person for public comment at hearings.
summary: Discussed draft rules of procedure for continuations and ex parte disclosures, which staff will revise before the November meeting. Reviewed the draft future land use map for the 2027 Winooski Comprehensive Plan, including the Gilbrook area. The applicants for 50 Park Street withdrew their Final Plan Review application.
decisions: Applicants withdrew their application for 50 Park Street, Final Plan Review.
Agreed that if an applicant does not appear at a public hearing and no continuation requests are submitted, the board will review the application, take public comment, and deliberate on its merits.
Agreed on a three-minute limit per person for public comment during public hearings.
Agreed to add a rule that after two continuation requests, or a request that would push the hearing past 120 days, the board will decide the application.

10/15/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: David Weissberger, Chair; Felipe Hoyos; Jordan Matte; Riley Livermore
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning
Guests Present: Kate Coffey
Call to Order by: David
Meeting Start Time: 6:30 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
David asked to add an ex parte communication disclosure after item VI. Motion by Felipe, 
seconded by Riley, to approve the agenda with David’s requested addition to the agenda. Voting: 
Unanimous. Motion carried.
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Jordan
Second: Felipe
Decision: Voting: Unanimous. Motion carried
Disclosure of Ex Parte Communications
David said that after reviewing the DRB Rules of Procedure, he found that board members must 
disclose any ex parte communications to any person outside of a regularly scheduled meeting. 
David said that Kate Coffey contacted the DRB members regarding the rules of procedure and 
50 Park Street. David said that he had copied Ravi in his response to Kate, which is in 
conformance with the rules of procedure.
Discussion/Approval: DRB Rules of Procedure 
Ravi gave an overview of the issue from the previous DRB meeting regarding the rules of 
procedure regarding continuances. Ravi said that he had the current DRB rules of procedure 
reviewed by the City attorney, and that the City attorney had given clarification on procedures for 
continuations and a review of the current rules of procedure. Ravi said that he has included in 
the meeting materials a markup of the current rules of procedure based on the City attorney’s 
review, as well as the DRB rules of procedure from nearby municipalities to facilitate 
discussion. Ravi said that the DRB should discuss how it wants to regard continuations when 
requested. Ravi said that after discussions, he will draft the rules of procedure for the City 
attorney to review before the DRB adopts it.
David reviewed the two hypothetical scenarios in which the question of a continuation would 
arise—(1) in which the applicant does not show up and does not give notice; and (2) in which 
the applicant does not show up, gives notice and requests a continuation. The board discussed 
the administrative burden of continuations and the helpfulness of flexibility. David asked for 
clarification about the City attorney’s remark about hearings that go beyond the 120 days as 
stated in statute, and about whether the board can deny continuation requests. Ravi said that a 
public hearing has to be scheduled within 120 days from when applications are considered 
complete. Ravi said that based on the City attorney’s comments, denying the initial continuation 
request may be legally questionable but denying a continuation request after one or two 
approved continuation requests would be less questionable.
David asked about the process for rendering a decision when the applicant isn’t present and no 
continuation requests were submitted, adding that the City attorney’s guidance says that 
applications must be ruled upon based on its merits even when the applicant isn’t present. The 
board came to consensus that if an applicant does not appear for a public hearing and no 
continuation requests, the board should review the application, take public comment and 
deliberate on the merits of the application. David suggested asking the City attorney if this 
scenario violates due process for the applicant.
David asked about what the board can do when continuation requests are submitted. Ravi 
reviewed the statute reference on hearing applications within 120 days of it being determined 
complete. Ravi and the board discussed the mechanics of continuation requests.
Riley asked if continuations are primarily because of the applicant. Ravi said that continuation 
requests typically stem from staff not having enough time to review the application completely, 
from the DRB not hearing enough public input if many people are in attendance, or from the 
board if it does not have enough information to determine the impacts of the development.
Riley asked about the administrative burden on continuation requests. Ravi said that for the 
most part, the burden is on the applicant to fulfill the requests from the DRB, and that only in 
extremely rare instances in his experience, continuations are approved because of issues 
beyond staff’s or the applicant’s control. Riley concluded that continuing an application 
indefinitely is in no one’s best interest.
David suggested adding in the rules of procedure that after two continuation requests or the 
continuation request would cause the hearing to occur after 120 days from when the application 
is determined complete, the DRB will adjudicate on the application. The board concurred with 
this suggestion, adding that this has enough flexibility. The board discussed when the 
continuation request should be provided. Ravi said he’d prefer to receive the request a week in 
advance.
David discussed references to ex parte communications and suggested adding language in the 
Rules of Procedure to address ex parte communications disclosures. Ravi suggested having all 
the necessary elements in the rules of procedure, so the board would not need to review 
external references for procedures. David noted the references to procedures in the Unified 
Land Use and Development Regulations (ULUDR) and the Conflict of Interest Policy, and 
suggested removing the procedural information in the ULUDR and adding any information in the 
ULUDR that is not in the Rules of Procedure into the Rules of Procedure.
Felipe asked about the service list that the City attorney mentioned. Ravi said that the Rules of 
Procedure does not have a reference to a service list, but that he has to furnish this for the 
record in case of appeals. Ravi said that he has to mail the decision to all attendees who 
attended the public hearing per statute.
Riley asked about limits to the amount of time for public comment. Ravi reviewed Shelburne’s 
Rules of Procedure on limits, and pointed out that the 10-minute limit in the Rules of Procedure 
is for the public comment at the beginning of a meeting for non-agenda items. Ravi said that in 
Shelburne, three minutes per person during public hearings is a rule of thumb that can be 
adjusted depending on the number of attendees, to make sure that everyone has the chance to 
provide comments. The board agreed on a three-minute limit per person for public comment 
during public hearings, and suggested clarifying the limitations of public comment in the rules of 
procedure.
Ravi said that he’ll revise the rules of procedure ahead of the meeting in November for the board 
to review and approve sooner rather than later.
Discussion: 2027 Winooski Comprehensive Plan – Land Use Section
Ravi reviewed the drafting phase of the Winooski Comprehensive Plan. Ravi gave an overview 
of the basis of the draft future land use map, and asked the board about their thoughts about the 
designations for Gilbrook. The board pointed out how wet the area highlighted as “Transition” 
are. Riley said that further development doesn’t seem in alignment with improving the 
connectivity of the community, since access would be from Colchester. David asked about the 
relationship between the future land use map and the zoning map. Ravi said that the future land 
use map and the zoning map have to be in alignment, and that any changes to the zoning map 
have to be based on the future land use map. David asked why the school and the parks are 
designated as developable. Ravi said that designations are based on the developability of the 
site not on its current status.
David asked about the timeline for developing the Comprehensive Plan. Ravi said he hopes to 
complete a draft by the end of the year. Ravi said that the survey on the current draft goals and 
objectives will be live until the end of the week. Ravi said that additional iterations of the goals 
and objectives will be circulated next month and that the board will have a chance to give 
comments on updated drafts.
City Updates
Ravi said that his main focus has been on the Comprehensive Plan drafting, that zoning permit 
applications have slowed down, and that the hotel and housing project at the end of Winooski 
Falls Way is making progress.
Other Business
Ravi said that the applicants for 50 Park Street have withdrawn their application and that this 
notice has been sent to all the adjoining property owners. Riley asked if the applicants would 
have to reapply in its entirety if they want to continue pursuing the project at 50 Park Street. Ravi 
said that the withdrawal only applies to Final Plan Review, and that the applicant can reapply for 
Final Plan Review within the validity of their Preliminary Plan Review decision, which expires at 
the end of May.
Adjourn
Motion by: Riley
Second: Felipe
Meeting End Time: 7:56 pm

connectivity of the community, since access would be from Colchester. David asked about the 
relationship between the future land use map and the zoning map. Ravi said that the future land 
use map and the zoning map have to be in alignment, and that any changes to the zoning map 
have to be based on the future land use map. David asked why the school and the parks are 
designated as developable. Ravi said that designations are based on the developability of the

David asked about the timeline for developing the Comprehensive Plan. Ravi said he hopes to 
complete a draft by the end of the year. Ravi said that the survey on the current draft goals and 
objectives will be live until the end of the week. Ravi said that additional iterations of the goals 
and objectives will be circulated next month and that the board will have a chance to give 
comments on updated drafts.
City Updates
Ravi said that his main focus has been on the Comprehensive Plan drafting, that zoning permit 
applications have slowed down, and that the hotel and housing project at the end of Winooski 
Falls Way is making progress.
Other Business
Ravi said that the applicants for 50 Park Street have withdrawn their application and that this 
notice has been sent to all the adjoining property owners. Riley asked if the applicants would 
have to reapply in its entirety if they want to continue pursuing the project at 50 Park Street. Ravi 
said that the withdrawal only applies to Final Plan Review, and that the applicant can reapply for 
Final Plan Review within the validity of their Preliminary Plan Review decision, which expires at 
the end of May.
